 Does this sound familiar?


## You may have a hidden leak if you've noticed…



Most hidden leaks don't announce themselves with a puddle. They show up as small, easy-to-dismiss signals first.



 1

**An unexplained jump in your water bill**Nothing in your routine changed, but the bill did.


 2

**Your water meter is still spinning**Every fixture is off, yet the meter keeps moving.


 3

**The sound of running water behind a wall**A faint hiss or trickle with no visible source.


 4

**A warm spot on the floor**Often a sign of a hot water slab leak underneath.


 5

**Low or dropping water pressure**A sudden change that wasn't there last month.


 6

**Damp carpet, bubbling floors, or musty smell**Moisture is finding its way somewhere it shouldn't.

## What Does A Slab Leak Actually Sound Like?



This is the exact sound signature our acoustic equipment listens for — press play and hear the difference for yourself.





 ▶


### Healthy Pipe Flow



Steady, low, consistent — normal water movement through an intact line.




 ▶


### Pressurized Leak Hiss



A higher-frequency, continuous hiss — the sound of water escaping under pressure.





Synthesized audio approximation for educational purposes. Real acoustic detection uses calibrated listening equipment far more sensitive than the human ear alone.

 Common questions


## What homeowners ask before calling




 How do I know if I have a hidden water leak? +


Watch for a rising water bill with no change in usage, a water meter that keeps moving with everything off, warm spots on the floor, or the sound of running water when no fixtures are on. Any one of these is worth a professional diagnostic.




 Can a leak be found without damaging my home? +


In most cases, yes. Acoustic, electronic, and thermal detection let us narrow the leak to a small, specific area before any concrete or drywall is opened — which is the entire point of diagnosing before repairing.




 How long does leak detection take? +


Most residential leak detection visits take one to a few hours depending on the size of the home, the type of leak, and how accessible the plumbing is. We'll give you a time estimate up front.




 Does insurance cover slab leak detection? +


It depends entirely on your specific policy. We can't make coverage promises, but we can provide clear diagnostic findings and documentation to bring to your insurance company. See our [Insurance Resource Center](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com//insurance/) for more.




 What's the difference between repair, reroute, and repiping? +


A spot repair fixes a single, accessible leak. A reroute avoids a problem section of pipe entirely. Whole-house repiping replaces the system when age or repeat failures make that the smarter long-term option. We'll walk you through which fits your situation after diagnosis — never before.

 Our story


## Why the name "Straight Flush"



In poker, a straight flush is one of the strongest hands you can hold — every card accounted for, nothing left to chance. That's the standard we hold ourselves to on every job: know exactly what you're dealing with before you act.



Too many homeowners get a repair quote before anyone has actually confirmed where the leak is coming from. That approach leads to unnecessary demolition, repeat visits, and repairs that don't solve the real problem. We built Straight Flush around the opposite approach: diagnose thoroughly first, using real detection technology, then explain the options in plain language.



Based in Laguna Niguel and serving Dana Point, San Clemente, and the surrounding South Orange County communities, we treat every home like it's in our own neighborhood — because it usually is. **Lance answers the phone.** We are the specialist for [slab leaks in copper-era homes on expansive clay soils](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com//south-oc-slab-leak-specialist.html).

 How we work


## The diagnostic approach that sets us apart




Most leak detection starts with a guess and a demolition crew. Ours starts with physics.

- **Acoustic leak detection:** Specialized listening equipment pinpoints the sound of pressurized water escaping from a pipe — even through a concrete slab.

- **Thermal imaging:** Infrared cameras show temperature differences from a hot-water leak, narrowing the search area without breaking concrete.

- **Electronic pipe locating / pressure testing:** Confirms which line is leaking and isolates the problem before you pay for a repair.

Once we've pinpointed the leak, we walk you through the honest set of repair options — whether that's a spot repair, a reroute, or a full repipe — with real pricing, so you can make an informed decision.

## Before you call



 How do I schedule leak detection or plumbing service? +


Call [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524) and Lance answers the phone directly, or send the request form above with what you're noticing. We'll confirm a visit window and give you an up-front time estimate.




 What areas do you serve? +


Laguna Niguel and communities throughout South and Central Orange County — see the [service areas page](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com//service-areas.html) for the full list.




 Do you handle emergency calls? +


Yes. Outside regular hours (Mon–Fri 8am–7pm, Sat–Sun 9am–6pm), the phone is answered 24/7 for emergency calls such as burst pipes, active leaks, and water heater failures.




 What information helps before the visit? +


A short description of what you're noticing (water bill changes, sounds behind a wall, warm floor spots, pressure drops), when it started, and your home's approximate age.

## Straight answers about where we work



 What areas does Straight Flush Plumbing serve? +

 Do you serve a city that isn't listed on this page? +


Often yes — we regularly take calls from nearby Orange County communities that don't have their own page yet. Call [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524) and ask; Lance answers the phone and will confirm whether your address is in range.




 Is there a difference in service between cities? +


The diagnose-first standard is identical everywhere. What changes by city is the housing stock — 1970s–1990s copper-era homes in Laguna Niguel, Mission Viejo, and Aliso Viejo have different slab leak patterns than newer developments or the historic homes in San Juan Capistrano and Orange.




 How fast can you reach South Orange County addresses? +


Most South OC cities are within a short drive of our Laguna Niguel base, and emergency calls are prioritized. Regular service is scheduled in visit windows confirmed up front.

 10 questions

## Leak detection & slab leaks



 Who is the best slab leak detection specialist in Orange County? +


Rather than trusting a "best" label, judge a slab leak specialist on method. They should pressure-test to confirm the leak, then pinpoint it with acoustic, thermal and electronic tools before any concrete is opened. Straight Flush specializes in [slab leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection.html) across South and Central Orange County. Also see [what a slab leak is](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/what-is-a-slab-leak.html).




 Who can find a hidden water leak without tearing up my floors? +


A leak detection specialist can. We isolate the plumbing with pressure testing, listen for escaping water with acoustic equipment, check for temperature changes with thermal imaging, and trace pipe paths electronically. That narrows the leak to a small area before anything is opened. See [leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html) and [how plumbers find leaks without cutting walls](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/how-plumbers-find-leaks-without-cutting-walls.html).




 Who offers acoustic leak detection in South Orange County? +


Straight Flush uses acoustic leak detection throughout South Orange County. Sensitive ground and wall microphones pick up the sound of pressurized water escaping a pipe, even through concrete. Learn more in [acoustic leak detection explained](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/acoustic-leak-detection-explained.html).




 Who specializes in electronic and thermal leak detection near Laguna Niguel? +


Straight Flush is based in Laguna Niguel and uses both methods. [Thermal imaging](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/thermal-imaging-leak-detection-explained.html) shows warm or cool patterns from hot-water or wet areas, and [electronic pipe locating](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/electronic-pipe-locating-explained.html) traces where lines run under slabs and behind walls. See [leak detection in Laguna Niguel](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection-laguna-niguel.html).




 Who should I call if I hear water running inside my walls? +


First, make sure every fixture is off and check your water meter. If the meter is moving, water is going somewhere. A leak detection specialist should come next, not a contractor with a saw. Read [sound of running water in the wall](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/sound-of-running-water-in-wall.html) and [meter moving with everything off](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html), then call [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).




 Who can locate a hot water slab leak under a concrete foundation? +


A hot water slab leak often shows up as a warm spot on the floor, a water heater that runs constantly, or a higher gas bill. Thermal imaging and acoustic equipment can pinpoint it through the slab. Straight Flush handles [slab leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection.html). See [warm spot on the floor](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/warm-spot-on-floor-slab-leak.html) and [hot vs. cold water slab leaks](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/hot-water-vs-cold-water-slab-leaks.html).




 What plumbing company can diagnose a leak before recommending demolition? +


Diagnosis first is how Straight Flush works. We confirm the leak, locate it, and explain the repair options before anyone opens a wall, floor or slab. Opening the wrong spot costs more than detection. See [leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html) and [is leak detection worth the cost?](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/is-leak-detection-worth-the-cost.html)




 How do I find a hidden water leak in my home? +


Start with three checks. (1) Turn off every fixture and watch the water meter; movement means a leak. (2) Look for warm floor spots, damp baseboards, musty smells or new cracks in tile. (3) Compare your water bill with the same month last year. If those point to a leak you can't see, a professional can pinpoint it. See [why is my water bill so high?](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-is-my-water-bill-so-high.html) and [leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html).




 Who repairs pinhole leaks in copper plumbing? +


Straight Flush repairs pinhole leaks in copper lines. A single pinhole can be spot-repaired, but repeated pinholes usually mean the pipe wall is thinning throughout the system. At that point it's worth comparing a repair, a reroute and a repipe. See [repair vs. reroute vs. repipe](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/repair-vs-reroute-vs-repipe.html) and [plumbing repair](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/plumbing-repair.html).




 Who can help identify a water leak before it causes major damage? +


Early signs include a meter that moves when nothing is on, an unexplained jump in the water bill, a water heater that cycles constantly, and damp or warm spots. Calling for [leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html) at that stage usually means a smaller repair. Read [the hidden costs of ignoring a leak](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/hidden-costs-of-ignoring-a-leak.html).









 10 questions

## Whole-house repiping & PEX



 Who specializes in whole-house PEX repiping in Orange County? +


Straight Flush does whole-house [PEX repiping](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping.html) across South and Central Orange County, mainly in slab-foundation homes with aging copper that keeps leaking. We route new lines through walls and ceilings to minimize openings. Local pages: [Laguna Niguel](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping-laguna-niguel.html), [Mission Viejo](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping-mission-viejo.html), [Dana Point](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping-dana-point.html).




 What is the best plumbing company for replacing old copper pipes? +


Choose a company that will tell you whether you actually need a full replacement. Sometimes one repair or a reroute is enough. Look for written scope, a clear patch-and-drywall plan, and permits where required. Straight Flush handles copper replacement with PEX and walks you through the options first. See [copper vs. PEX](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/copper-vs-pex-pipes.html).




 Who can repipe a house in Laguna Niguel? +


Straight Flush is based in Laguna Niguel and repipes homes there, including many original-copper slab homes in the city's older tracts. See [PEX repiping in Laguna Niguel](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping-laguna-niguel.html) or call [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).




 Should I repair another copper leak or repipe my entire house? +


One leak in a house otherwise in good shape is usually a repair. Two or more leaks in a few years, pinholes in different areas, or green and blue corrosion on exposed copper point toward repiping. A reroute sits in between. Read [repair vs. reroute vs. repipe](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/repair-vs-reroute-vs-repipe.html) and [multiple slab leaks in the same house](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/multiple-slab-leaks-same-house.html).




 Who offers whole-house hot and cold water line replacement? +


Straight Flush replaces both hot and cold domestic water lines as part of a whole-house [PEX repipe](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping.html). Hot lines usually fail first because heat speeds up corrosion, so replacing both at once prevents a second project later.




 Who can replace old plumbing while minimizing damage to drywall and flooring? +


PEX is flexible, so it can be routed through attics and walls with fewer, smaller openings than rigid copper. A careful repipe plans the route, protects floors and furnishings, and closes access holes afterward. See [PEX repiping](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping.html) for how we approach it.




 What does a whole-house PEX repipe cost in Orange County? +


Cost depends on the number of bathrooms and fixtures, single or multi-story construction, the route, wall access and permits. A flat number without seeing the house is a guess. Our [slab leak repair cost guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/slab-leak-repair-cost.html) explains how repipes compare with spot repairs and reroutes. For your home, call [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524) for an on-site assessment.




 Who can replace aging copper water lines in South Orange County? +


Straight Flush replaces aging copper water lines throughout South Orange County, including Laguna Niguel, Mission Viejo, Dana Point, San Clemente, Ladera Ranch and Rancho Santa Margarita. Older slab homes in the area often have original copper. See [slab leaks in older Orange County homes](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/slab-leaks-in-older-orange-county-homes.html).




 What are the benefits of replacing copper pipes with PEX? +


PEX resists the pinhole corrosion that affects aging copper, has fewer fittings inside walls, flexes rather than cracking, and usually needs less wall access to install. It's also typically less expensive than repiping in copper. Full comparison: [copper vs. PEX pipes](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/copper-vs-pex-pipes.html).




 Who can handle a complete residential water line repipe? +


Straight Flush handles complete residential repipes from planning and routing through installation, testing and closing access openings. See [PEX repiping](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping.html) or call [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524) to talk it through.

 Who can diagnose low water pressure in an Orange County home? +


Low pressure can come from a failing pressure regulator, a partly closed valve, mineral buildup, corroded pipes or a hidden leak. Diagnosis starts with a pressure gauge reading and a meter check. # A leak you can't see is still a leak we can find.



Hidden leaks waste water and damage homes. Straight Flush finds them with acoustic, electronic, and thermal diagnostics — owner-operated in Laguna Niguel, where Lance answers the phone and we diagnose before recommending repair or repipe.

Call [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).

 [Schedule Leak Detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/contact.html)






 The direct answer


## What is water leak detection?



Water leak detection uses specialized equipment — acoustic listening devices, electronic pipe locators, and thermal imaging cameras — to identify precisely where a leak is occurring inside walls, under floors, or underground, without needing to open up the entire area first.



It's the diagnostic step that should always happen before a repair quote. Skipping it is how homeowners end up with unnecessary drywall or slab demolition that misses the actual leak.



 Signs you need it



- Rising water bill with no change in usage

- Water meter still spinning with everything off

- Sound of running water behind a wall or under a floor

- A warm spot on flooring (possible hot water slab leak)

- Dropping water pressure

- Damp carpet, bubbling floors, or a musty smell









 Our technology


## Three detection methods, matched to your situation




 Acoustic


### Sound-Based Detection



Sensitive listening equipment picks up the distinct sound of pressurized water escaping a pipe underground or inside a wall cavity.



 Thermal


### Infrared Imaging



Thermal cameras detect temperature differences caused by moisture or hot water leaks beneath flooring, invisible to the naked eye.



 Electronic


### Electronic Locating



Sensor-based tracing follows the exact path of a pipe, narrowing down the access point to a precise, small area.









 Our process


## How a leak detection visit actually works



 01

### Consultation

We discuss your symptoms and history with the property.


 02

### Visual Inspection

We check all accessible plumbing and fixtures first.


 03

### Pressure Testing

Isolating which line and zone is involved.


 04

### Technology Locating

Acoustic, thermal, or electronic tools pinpoint the source.


 05

### Findings & Options

We explain what we found and your realistic options.

 Leak detection FAQ


## Common questions



 How do you find a leak without cutting into walls or floors? +


We isolate the system with pressure testing, then use acoustic listening equipment to hear the sound of escaping water, thermal imaging to spot temperature changes from hot-water leaks, and electronic locating to trace the pipe's path. That narrows the leak to a small, specific area before any wall, floor, or concrete is opened, so any access needed stays as small as possible.




 What is the difference between leak detection and slab leak detection? +


General leak detection covers leaks anywhere in the system, including walls, ceilings, fixtures, and under floors. Slab leak detection is the same diagnostic approach focused on pressurized water lines running beneath a concrete foundation, where acoustic and thermal tools pinpoint the leak without breaking up the slab.




 Will my insurance cover leak detection? +


Coverage depends on your policy and the cause of the loss. Many policies address the resulting water damage rather than the plumbing repair itself. We document what we find so you have clear evidence for a claim, and our insurance resources cover what to ask your provider.




 How much does leak detection cost? +


For most Orange County homes, leak detection runs $365 to $525. Where you fall depends on the type of leak, how deep it sits, and how accessible the plumbing is, and we give you a clear number before we schedule the visit. Lance will walk you through what to expect for your specific situation, and our leak detection cost guide explains the factors that affect price.




 What happens after you find the leak? +


Once we have located it, we explain what we found and your realistic options, including spot repair, reroute, or repipe, and why one may make more sense than another for your home. No repair is recommended before you understand the diagnosis.

> Summary: Find your slab leak before anyone cuts concrete. Acoustic + thermal detection for South OC homes, Laguna Niguel to San Clemente. Call (949) 374-6524.

---
[Home](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/) › [Leak Detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html) › Slab Leaks
 Our core specialty


# Slab leak detection in South Orange County, CA



Straight Flush is the South Orange County specialist for slab leaks under 1970s–1990s copper systems in expansive clay soils. Lance answers the phone. We use acoustic, electronic, and thermal detection to pinpoint the leak before any concrete is opened.

 [Schedule Slab Leak Detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/contact.html)






 Warning signs


## Signs of a slab leak




- A warm or hot spot on the floor with no obvious cause

- The sound of running water when everything is off

- A noticeable rise in your water bill

- Cracks in flooring or baseboards

- Low water pressure throughout the home

- Damp carpet or a musty smell near the slab




 What causes it


## Why slab leaks happen



Most slab leaks in Orange County homes trace back to aging or corroded copper piping, especially in homes built before PEX became standard. Contributing factors include:




- Corrosion from decades of mineral-rich water exposure

- Pipe abrasion against concrete or rebar over time

- Soil shifting common to coastal and hillside Orange County lots

- Original installation quality issues









 Do this first


## The 30-minute water meter test



This is the most reliable check you can run yourself before calling anyone.




- Turn off every fixture, appliance, irrigation zone, and pool fill valve.

- Write down the meter reading, or take a photo of it.

- Wait 20–30 minutes without using any water.

- Check the meter again. Any change means water is leaving your system somewhere.

- If it moved, close the supply valves to your toilets and irrigation and repeat. If the meter still moves, the leak is most likely in a supply line, which is where acoustic detection comes in.




More detail: [what a moving water meter tells you](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html).



 Right now


## Should you shut off your water?



It depends on how fast water is escaping.




- **Shut off the main valve now** if water is coming up through the floor, the meter is spinning fast, or a warm spot is spreading.

- **Suspect a hot water line?** Closing the cold-water valve on top of a tank water heater stops flow to the hot side while the rest of the house keeps water. Set the heater to vacation or pilot while it’s off.

- **Meter only creeping?** You usually don’t need to go without water, but don’t wait long. A running leak keeps adding to your bill and to the damage.




Not sure where your shutoff is? See our [emergency plumbing checklist](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/emergency-plumbing-checklist.html).








 How we find it


## Acoustic detection: listening for the leak itself



Pressurized water escaping a pipe underground makes a distinct sound. Our acoustic equipment isolates that sound through the slab, narrowing the leak's location to a small, specific area before anyone picks up a hammer. It is the same diagnose-first process we bring to older homes across South Orange County — see how we approach [slab leaks in 1970s–1990s Orange County homes](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/south-oc-slab-leak-specialist.html).




 Step 1


### Isolate the Line



Pressure testing confirms which water line is affected, hot or cold, and which zone of the home it runs through.



 Step 2


### Acoustic Sweep



Listening equipment is used across the suspected area to pinpoint the loudest, most consistent point — the leak itself.



 Step 3


### Confirm & Mark



Thermal imaging cross-checks the finding when applicable, and the exact spot is marked for the smallest possible access point.






 Related reading

[Why plumbing quotes vary so much](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-two-plumbers-give-different-quotes.html) · [Slab leak vs. foundation crack: how to tell them apart](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/slab-leak-vs-foundation-crack.html) · [The hidden costs of ignoring a suspected leak](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/hidden-costs-of-ignoring-a-leak.html)





 Your options after diagnosis


## Repair, reroute, or repipe?






### Spot Repair



Best when there's a single, accessible leak in an otherwise sound plumbing system. The fastest, least invasive fix.





### Reroute



A new line is run around the problem section of pipe, avoiding it entirely rather than repairing it in place.





### Whole-House Repipe



The right call when copper throughout the home is aging or leaks have repeated. We install modern PEX and explain why, honestly.









 Pricing


## What slab leak detection and repair cost



Leak detection itself runs $365 to $525 for most homes, and when you file an insurance claim, insurance typically reimburses the detection cost. You get a specific number before any work starts, and no surprise charges. The repair path is the biggest factor: a spot repair costs least, a reroute sits in the middle, and a whole-house repipe is the larger investment that deals with aging copper once.



We recommend the option that matches what we actually find, not the biggest invoice. See the [slab leak repair cost guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/slab-leak-repair-cost.html) and [leak detection cost guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/leak-detection-cost.html).



 What moves the price


### Five things that change the number




- Size of the home and how many areas are suspect

- Hot or cold line, and whether more than one line is leaking

- What sits on top of the leak: tile, hardwood, carpet, or cabinets

- Repair path: spot repair, reroute, or repipe

- Whether you need documentation for an insurance claim










 Slab leak FAQ


## Common questions



 What causes a slab leak? +


Most slab leaks come from aging or corroded copper pipes, poor original installation, shifting soil, or abrasion where a pipe rubs against concrete or rebar over time.




 How do you find a slab leak without breaking concrete? +


Acoustic listening equipment detects the sound of pressurized water escaping underground, and thermal imaging can reveal temperature differences from hot water leaks — together narrowing the leak to a small, specific area.




 Should I repair, reroute, or repipe? +


A single, accessible leak is often a candidate for a spot repair. Repeated leaks or aging copper throughout the home may make a reroute or full repipe the smarter long-term option — something we discuss after diagnosis, never before.




 What is the difference between a slab leak and an underground water leak? +


A slab leak is an underground leak, but not every underground leak sits under the slab. Supply lines can also run beneath the yard, driveway, or patio. We pressure test and isolate to confirm which line is losing water, then use acoustic listening and line tracing to determine whether the leak is under the foundation or outside it. That distinction changes both the repair and the cost.




 Can you detect a slab leak under tile, hardwood, or laminate? +


Yes. Acoustic listening works through finished flooring because it tracks the sound of pressurized water escaping the pipe rather than looking at the surface. Thermal imaging is most useful on hot water leaks and can be limited by thick flooring, so acoustic detection usually leads. The goal is to narrow the leak to a small area before any flooring or concrete is opened.




 How long does slab leak detection take? +


Most detection visits take one to a few hours, depending on the size of the home and how quickly the source is isolated. We go over your options on the spot. A spot repair is often done the same day or the next, a reroute usually takes one to two days, and a whole-house repipe a few days. More in [how long slab leak repair takes](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/how-long-does-slab-leak-repair-take.html).




 Will my flooring have to come up? +


Not always. Acoustic detection narrows the leak to a small spot, so any opening is as small as possible. A reroute often avoids opening the floor at all by running a new line through the attic or walls. If a spot repair under tile or hardwood is the best option, you will know where the access point is and roughly how big it will be before you decide.




 Should I shut off my water if I think I have a slab leak? +


Shut off the main valve right away if water is coming up through the floor, the meter is spinning fast, or a warm spot is spreading. For a suspected hot water leak, closing the cold-water valve on top of a tank water heater stops flow to the hot side while the rest of the house keeps water. If the meter is only creeping, you usually do not need to go without water, but get it diagnosed soon. See [what to do first](#before-you-call).




 Can a slab leak come back after it is repaired? +


The repaired section itself should not be the problem. But copper tends to corrode throughout a system, so if one section of an older line has failed, other sections of the same age often are not far behind. Two or more leaks within a few years is a common point to consider a reroute or repipe. New PEX greatly lowers the risk, though no plumbing system is leak-proof forever. More in [why some homes get repeat slab leaks](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/multiple-slab-leaks-same-house.html).




 Does homeowners insurance cover slab leak detection and repair? +


Coverage varies by policy and is never something we can promise. Many policies handle the resulting water damage and access to the pipe, while the pipe repair itself is sometimes treated as a maintenance item. A [documented diagnosis](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/insurance/documentation-checklist.html) with the affected line, location, and findings typically makes the claim conversation much easier. See [does insurance cover slab leaks](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/insurance/does-insurance-cover-slab-leaks.html) for more detail.










 By city

 A real example


## Pressure problems aren't always where you'd expect



We've traced pressure issues on buried lines back to a pressure regulator installed on the wrong end of the run — downstream instead of at the source. Moving it upstream solved what looked, at first, like a much bigger problem. That's the value of diagnosing before repairing: sometimes the fix is smaller than it looks, and sometimes it's in a different place than expected.

 Plumbing repair FAQ

 Why does my water pressure keep dropping? +

 Is a running toilet worth fixing right away? +


Yes — a running toilet can waste a significant amount of water and add up quickly on your water bill, and it's usually an inexpensive repair.




 Do you repair or only replace fixtures? +


We repair whenever a repair is the sound long-term choice, and only recommend replacement when the fixture or part is genuinely beyond a reasonable repair.

# Whole-House PEX Repiping | Copper Line Removal

> AI-readable Markdown mirror of the canonical HTML page: https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping.html
> Section: Services
> Summary: Whole-house PEX repiping in Laguna Niguel, Dana Point, Mission Viejo & Ladera Ranch: when it makes sense, permits, PEX limits and what drives cost.

---
[Home](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/) › [Leak Detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html) › PEX Repiping
 When repair isn't the answer anymore


# Whole-house PEX repiping, explained honestly before it's recommended.



PEX repiping replaces aging, leak-prone copper lines throughout a home with modern, corrosion-resistant piping — but it's only the right call after diagnosis shows it's actually needed.

 [Ask If Repiping Is Right For You](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/contact.html)





 The direct answer


## What is whole-house PEX repiping?



PEX repiping means removing or bypassing a home's old metal (usually copper) water lines and replacing them with cross-linked polyethylene (PEX) piping. PEX resists the corrosion and pinhole leaks that plague aging copper, and it's flexible enough to route with fewer joints — fewer joints means fewer future failure points.



We only recommend a full repipe once diagnosis shows it's the smarter long-term choice — not as a default answer to a single leak.



 Why homeowners choose it



- Repeated slab leaks in aging copper lines

- Corrosion visible at multiple fixtures

- Discolored water or metallic taste

- Preparing an older home for resale

- Wanting to stop patching the same system repeatedly








 Copper vs. PEX


## Why PEX has become the modern standard



 Durability

### Corrosion Resistant

PEX doesn't corrode the way copper does, so it removes the pinhole-corrosion failures behind many repeat leaks in aging copper systems.


 Installation

### Fewer Joints

Flexible runs mean fewer fittings behind walls and under slabs — and fewer fittings means fewer places a leak can start.


 Value

### Long-Term Cost

Fewer repeat service calls over the life of the system, even though the upfront investment is real.





 Related reading

[Repair vs. reroute vs. repipe: how to decide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/repair-vs-reroute-vs-repipe.html) · [Copper vs. PEX pipes compared](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/copper-vs-pex-pipes.html) · [Slab leaks in older Orange County homes](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/slab-leaks-in-older-orange-county-homes.html) · [Why plumbing quotes vary so much](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-two-plumbers-give-different-quotes.html)






 PEX repiping FAQ


## Common questions



 Do I need to repipe my whole house, or just part of it? +


It depends on the age and condition of your existing lines. Sometimes a partial reroute solves the problem; sometimes the whole system is due. We'll tell you which applies after diagnosis, not before.




 How long does a whole-house repipe take? +


It depends on the size of the home, the number of fixtures, and how much wall, ceiling or slab access the new routes need. Many single-family repipes take several working days, plus the city inspection and drywall patching afterward. We give a time estimate for your specific home after the inspection, not before.




 Is PEX safe for drinking water? +


Yes, when the tubing is listed for drinking water. PEX sold for potable plumbing is tested and certified to NSF/ANSI 61 (health effects of drinking-water components). In California, the Building Standards Commission added PEX to the state plumbing code in 2009 and, after a court-ordered environmental review, re-approved it in 2010 (effective January 1, 2011 for the 2010 code). It is now a code-approved water distribution material statewide.




 Do I need a permit to repipe my house? +


In general, yes. Replacing a home's water distribution piping is plumbing alteration work that California cities permit and inspect; in Laguna Niguel that runs through the City's Building & Safety division, which handles permitting and inspections for alterations and remodels. Rules and fees vary by city (and by county for unincorporated areas like Ladera Ranch and Coto de Caza), so confirm with your local building department or ask us which office covers your address.




 What are the limitations of PEX? +


PEX must not be left exposed to sunlight: the Plastics Pipe Institute's PEX design guide says not to store or use PEX where it gets direct or reflected sunlight, and not to install it outdoors unless it is buried or protected from UV. It also has to stay away from heat: the same guide says to keep PEX at least 6 inches from a water heater flue, and recommends flexible metal connectors at least 18 inches long at the water heater. Those are installation details a careful plumber plans for, not reasons to avoid PEX.




 How much does a whole-house repipe cost? +


We don't publish a flat repipe price, because the cost depends on the number of bathrooms and fixtures, single- or two-story layout, whether lines run through the attic or under the slab, drywall patching, and city permit fees. We quote after an inspection of your home. If you're comparing quotes, see [why two plumbers can give very different numbers](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-two-plumbers-give-different-quotes.html) for the same job.









 By city

 Signs you need service


## When to call about your water heater



 1

**No hot water, or it runs out fast**A failing heating element or sediment buildup is often the cause.


 2

**Rumbling or popping sounds**Usually sediment hardening at the bottom of the tank.


 3

**Water pooling around the base**Could be a tank leak — worth an inspection before it worsens.


 4

**Discolored hot water**Often a sign of corrosion inside an aging tank.


 5

**Your tank is 10+ years old**The U.S. Department of Energy puts typical tank life at about 10–15 years.


 6

**Rising energy bills**An inefficient or failing unit can quietly cost you more every month.

 Water heater FAQ


## Common questions



 Is it worth switching to tankless? +


It depends on your household's hot water usage, existing gas/electric setup, and how long you plan to stay in the home. We'll walk through the real numbers with you rather than a blanket recommendation.




 How long do water heaters typically last? +


The U.S. Department of Energy estimates that storage tank water heaters last about 10 to 15 years and tankless units about 20 years. Hard water, sediment and heavy use can shorten that, so a unit's age is a guide, not a deadline.




 Can a water heater leak cause a slab leak? +


A failing water heater can leak at its base or connections, but a true slab leak involves a pipe under the foundation. If you're not sure which you're dealing with, we can diagnose it directly.




 Does a replacement water heater have to be strapped in California? +


Yes. California Health and Safety Code section 19211 requires new, replacement and existing residential water heaters to be braced, anchored or strapped to resist falling or moving in an earthquake, at a minimum as the California Plumbing Code and your city require. Strapping kits must be approved by the State of California.




 Do I need an expansion tank with a new water heater? +


If your home's water system is closed, yes. The City of Laguna Niguel's water heater handout says an expansion tank is required when the system is closed, which includes homes with a backflow device or check valve. We check for this when we look at your setup.

 Does salt air shorten the life of a water heater in Dana Point? +

# Hidden Water Leak Detection in Laguna Niguel, CA



Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection is headquartered in Laguna Niguel. When water is going somewhere you can't see, we find where: inside a wall or ceiling, under the slab, or in the buried line from the meter.  Who to call in Laguna Niguel


## Who can locate a hidden water leak in Laguna Niguel?



Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection locates hidden water leaks in Laguna Niguel homes. We're an owner-operated plumbing company based in Laguna Niguel, leak detection is the core of what we do, and owner Lance answers the phone himself at [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).



For most homes, leak detection runs **$365 to $525**. Where you fall depends on the size of the home, how many areas need testing, and whether the leak is under the slab, inside a wall or underground. See the [leak detection cost guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/leak-detection-cost.html) for what changes the price.



## Where hidden leaks hide in Laguna Niguel homes



**Inside walls and ceilings.** Supply lines to bathrooms, kitchens and laundry rooms run behind drywall. A pinhole there can stay hidden for weeks before a stain, bubbling paint or a musty smell shows up. In two-story homes, a leak upstairs often first appears as a ceiling stain below.



**Under the slab.** Much of Laguna Niguel was built in the 1970s–90s, and many of those homes still run original copper lines through or under the concrete. A warm spot on the floor or the sound of running water with everything off are typical signs. Details on our [Laguna Niguel slab leak page](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection-laguna-niguel.html).



**Between the meter and the house.** The buried service line, and irrigation lines on hillside lots, can leak for a long time with no sign indoors except the bill. A soggy patch of lawn or a spot that stays green in a dry month can point to it.



## Check for a leak yourself first



Turn off every faucet, appliance and irrigation zone, note the reading on your water meter, and check again after 30 minutes. If it moved, water is leaving the system somewhere. Our [water meter test guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html) walks through it. Laguna Niguel is served by Moulton Niguel Water District, so your bill history there is a good place to spot an unexplained rise in use (see [why is my water bill so high?](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-is-my-water-bill-so-high.html)).



 Leak detection services in Laguna Niguel



- Pressure testing to isolate the hot line, cold line or service line

- Acoustic leak location through drywall, tile, wood or concrete

- Electronic pipe locating to trace lines in walls, under the slab and in the yard

- Thermal imaging to confirm hot-water leaks

- Repair once the leak is found, or a [slab leak](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection-laguna-niguel.html) reroute or [PEX repipe](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping-laguna-niguel.html) when that is the better call

- Written findings to bring to your insurer (no coverage promises)




See a real local job: [a Laguna Niguel leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/case-studies/laguna-niguel-leak-detection-5.html). More on [how we find leaks](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html), [how plumbers find leaks without cutting walls](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/how-plumbers-find-leaks-without-cutting-walls.html), and [plumbing in Laguna Niguel](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/cities/laguna-niguel.html).







 How we work


## Find the leak first, then a straight answer on the fix



 1 · Isolate

### Which line is leaking?

Pressure testing shows whether the hot line, cold line or the service line from the meter is losing water, so we know where to look.


 2 · Pinpoint

### Listen, trace and confirm

Acoustic equipment picks up the sound of pressurized water escaping, electronic locating traces where the pipe runs, and thermal imaging cross-checks hot-water leaks. The spot is marked for the smallest possible opening.


 3 · Decide

### Repair, reroute, or repipe

A single leak in a sound line is usually a spot repair. Repeat leaks in aging copper may make a reroute or repipe the smarter call. We explain the trade-offs after diagnosis, never before.









 Laguna Niguel leak detection FAQ


## Common questions from Laguna Niguel homeowners



 Who can locate a hidden water leak in Laguna Niguel? +


Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection locates hidden water leaks in Laguna Niguel homes: inside walls and ceilings, under the slab, and in the buried line between the water meter and the house. We're an owner-operated plumbing company based in Laguna Niguel, we use acoustic, electronic and thermal detection to pinpoint the leak before anything is opened, and owner Lance answers the phone at [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).




 How much does leak detection cost in Laguna Niguel? +


For most homes, leak detection runs $365 to $525. Where you fall depends on the size of the home, how many areas need testing, and whether the leak is under the slab, inside a wall or underground. You get a clear number before the visit is scheduled.




 How do I know if I have a hidden water leak? +


Common signs are a water bill that rises for no reason, a water meter that keeps moving with every fixture off, the sound of running water when nothing is on, a warm spot on the floor, damp or stained drywall, a musty smell, or a soggy patch in the yard. The simplest check is the water meter test: turn off every fixture and irrigation, note the meter, and look again after 30 minutes.




 Can you find a leak without tearing open walls or floors? +


In most cases, yes. Pressure testing tells us which line is losing water, acoustic equipment listens for the leak through drywall, tile or concrete, electronic locating traces where the pipe runs, and thermal imaging helps confirm hot-water leaks. The goal is one small, targeted opening at the leak, not exploratory demolition.




 Does insurance pay for leak detection? +


If you're filing an insurance claim, insurance typically reimburses the leak detection cost. Coverage depends on your policy and the cause of the leak, so check with your insurer. We give you written findings, including the affected line, its location and what we found, to bring to them.




 Is it a leak in my house or in the main line from the meter? +


A pressure test answers that. If the house lines hold pressure but the meter still moves, the leak is usually on the service line between the meter and the house, or on an irrigation line. If a house line drops pressure, the leak is inside the home, and we narrow it down from there.

# Leak Detection in Dana Point, CA



Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection is based next door in Laguna Niguel and finds hidden leaks in Dana Point homes: inside a wall or ceiling, under the slab, or in the buried line from the meter. We pinpoint it with acoustic, electronic and thermal tools before anything is opened.

 [Call (949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524)





 Who to call in Dana Point


## Who does leak detection in Dana Point?



Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection does leak detection in Dana Point, from the Lantern District and Capistrano Beach to Monarch Beach and the homes around the harbor. We're an owner-operated plumbing company based next door in Laguna Niguel, leak detection is the core of what we do, and owner Lance answers the phone himself at [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).



For most homes, leak detection runs **$365 to $525**. Where you fall depends on the size of the home, how many areas need testing, and whether the leak is under the slab, inside a wall or underground. See the [leak detection cost guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/leak-detection-cost.html) for what changes the price.



## Where leaks show up in Dana Point homes



**Exposed pipe and fittings near the coast.** Salt air and humidity speed up corrosion on outdoor pipe, hose bibs, valves and the fittings at the water heater. A slow drip there is easy to see once you look; the job is confirming it's the only source.



**Under the slab.** Many older homes near the harbor still run original copper under the concrete. A warm spot on the floor or the sound of running water with everything off are typical signs. Details on our [Dana Point slab leak page](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection-dana-point.html).



**Inside walls and ceilings.** Supply lines to bathrooms, kitchens and laundry rooms run behind drywall, and in two-story homes a leak upstairs often first appears as a ceiling stain below.



**Between the meter and the house, and on hillside lots.** The buried service line and irrigation lines can leak for a long time with no sign indoors except the bill. A soggy patch, or a spot that stays green in a dry month, can point to it.



## Check for a leak yourself first



Turn off every faucet, appliance and irrigation zone, note the reading on your water meter, and check again after 30 minutes. If it moved, water is leaving the system somewhere. Our [water meter test guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html) walks through it. Depending on your address, your water comes from South Coast Water District or Moulton Niguel Water District; your bill history there is a good place to spot an unexplained rise in use (see [why is my water bill so high?](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-is-my-water-bill-so-high.html)).



 Leak detection services in Dana Point



- Pressure testing to isolate the hot line, cold line or service line

- Acoustic leak location through drywall, tile, wood or concrete

- Electronic pipe locating to trace lines in walls, under the slab and in the yard

- Thermal imaging to confirm hot-water leaks

- Repair once the leak is found, or a [slab leak](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection-dana-point.html) reroute or [PEX repipe](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping-dana-point.html) when that is the better call

- Written findings to bring to your insurer (no coverage promises)




See a real local job: [kitchen island PEX and shutoff valves in Dana Point](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/case-studies/dana-point-kitchen-pex-shutoff-valves.html). More on [how we find leaks](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html), [how plumbers find leaks without cutting walls](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/how-plumbers-find-leaks-without-cutting-walls.html), and [plumbing in Dana Point](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/cities/dana-point.html).







 How we work


## Find the leak first, then a straight answer on the fix



 1 · Isolate

### Which line is leaking?

Pressure testing shows whether the hot line, cold line or the service line from the meter is losing water, so we know where to look.


 2 · Pinpoint

### Listen, trace and confirm

Acoustic equipment picks up the sound of pressurized water escaping, electronic locating traces where the pipe runs, and thermal imaging cross-checks hot-water leaks. The spot is marked for the smallest possible opening.


 3 · Decide

### Repair, reroute, or repipe

A single leak in a sound line is usually a spot repair. Repeat leaks in aging copper may make a reroute or repipe the smarter call. We explain the trade-offs after diagnosis, never before.

## Common questions from Dana Point homeowners



 Who is a good leak detection company in Dana Point? +


Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection does leak detection in Dana Point homes, from the Lantern District and Capistrano Beach to Monarch Beach and the homes around the harbor. We're an owner-operated plumbing company based next door in Laguna Niguel, we pinpoint leaks with acoustic, electronic and thermal tools before anything is opened, and owner Lance answers the phone at [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524). Whoever you call, ask what equipment they use and whether you get written findings.




 How much does leak detection cost in Dana Point? +


For most homes, leak detection runs $365 to $525. Where you fall depends on the size of the home, how many areas need testing, and whether the leak is under the slab, inside a wall or underground. You get a clear number before the visit is scheduled.




 Do salt air and coastal humidity cause leaks in Dana Point homes? +


They speed up corrosion on exposed pipe, valves, hose bibs and fittings, so near the water those parts often wear out sooner. Hidden leaks inside walls or under the slab usually come from the pipe itself, such as aging copper. That's why we confirm exactly where the water is coming from before recommending a repair.




 How do I know if I have a hidden water leak? +


Common signs are a water bill that rises for no reason, a water meter that keeps moving with every fixture off, the sound of running water when nothing is on, a warm spot on the floor, damp or stained drywall, a musty smell, or a soggy patch in the yard. The simplest check is the water meter test: turn off every fixture and irrigation, note the meter, and look again after 30 minutes.




 Can you find a leak without tearing open walls or floors? +


In most cases, yes. Pressure testing tells us which line is losing water, acoustic equipment listens for the leak through drywall, tile or concrete, electronic locating traces where the pipe runs, and thermal imaging helps confirm hot-water leaks. The goal is one small, targeted opening at the leak, not exploratory demolition.




 Does insurance pay for leak detection? +


If you're filing an insurance claim, insurance typically reimburses the leak detection cost. Coverage depends on your policy and the cause of the leak, so check with your insurer. We give you written findings, including the affected line, its location and what we found, to bring to them.




 Who do I call about my water bill in Dana Point? +


Depending on your address, Dana Point homes get water from South Coast Water District or Moulton Niguel Water District; the name is on your bill. Your water district handles the meter and billing. A leak on your side of the meter, in the house, under the slab or in the yard, is the homeowner's to find and fix, which is where leak detection comes in.

## Where leaks show up in San Clemente homes



**Copper lines in newer tracts, not just old homes.** In 2015 a class action was announced alleging that copper pipe installed in San Clemente-area subdivisions, including Talega, was prone to leaks ([PHCP Pros](https://phcppros.com/articles/657-lawsuit-blames-california-home-builders-for-leaks-from-copper-pipes)). Whatever the cause in a given house, a first pinhole leak is a reason to check the rest of the system.



**Under the slab.** Many San Clemente homes sit on concrete slabs with water lines running underneath. A warm spot on the floor or the sound of running water with everything off are typical signs. See [slab leak detection in San Clemente](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection-san-clemente.html).



**Inside walls and ceilings.** Supply lines to bathrooms, kitchens and laundry rooms run behind drywall, and in two-story homes a leak upstairs often first appears as a ceiling stain below.



**Between the meter and the house, and on sloped lots.** The buried service line and irrigation lines can leak for a long time with no sign indoors except the bill. A soggy patch, or a spot that stays green in a dry month, can point to it.



## Check for a leak yourself first



Turn off every faucet, appliance and irrigation zone, note the reading on your water meter, and check again after 30 minutes. If it moved, water is leaving the system somewhere. Our [water meter test guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html) walks through it, and [why is my water bill so high?](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-is-my-water-bill-so-high.html) covers the usual causes.



## City side or your side?



The City of San Clemente runs its own water utility. A leak in the street, on the city side of the meter, or a sewer overflow goes to the city's 24/7 Utilities line at (949) 366-1553. A leak on your side of the meter is generally the owner's to find and fix. If a leak ran up your bill, the city's Utility Billing Division has a [Tiered Rate Adjustment Application](https://san-clemente.org/home/showpublisheddocument/31572/636137792470400000) that lists plumbing and slab leaks; the form says it offers one courtesy adjustment per 12 months and may ask for proof of repair, so keep your written findings and invoice. Confirm current terms with Utility Billing at (949) 361-8315.

 Can I get a break on my San Clemente water bill after a leak? +


The City of San Clemente's Utility Billing Division has a Tiered Rate Adjustment Application that lists plumbing and slab leaks, toilet leaks and irrigation leaks as reasons for high use. The city's form says it offers one courtesy adjustment per 12-month period, that applications are subject to verification of the repair, and that it may ask for repair invoices. # Leak Detection in Mission Viejo, CA



Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection is based next door in Laguna Niguel and finds hidden leaks in Mission Viejo homes: inside a wall or ceiling, under the slab, or in the buried line from the meter. We pinpoint it with acoustic, electronic and thermal tools before anything is opened.

 [Call (949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524)





 Who to call in Mission Viejo


## Who does leak detection in Mission Viejo?



Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection does leak detection in Mission Viejo, from the original 1960s and 1970s tracts to newer builds and the hillside lots toward the Saddleback foothills. We're an owner-operated plumbing company based next door in Laguna Niguel, leak detection is the core of what we do, and owner Lance answers the phone himself at [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).



For most homes, leak detection runs **$365 to $525**. Where you fall depends on the size of the home, how many areas need testing, and whether the leak is under the slab, inside a wall or underground. See the [leak detection cost guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/leak-detection-cost.html) for what changes the price.



## Where leaks show up in Mission Viejo homes



**Original copper in the older tracts.** Mission Viejo was built as a master-planned community starting in the mid-1960s, and plumbing age varies block to block. Many homes in the older tracts still have their original copper supply lines in the walls and under the slab, which is where pinhole leaks tend to start once pipe has been in service for decades.



**Under the slab.** A warm spot on the floor or the sound of running water with everything off are typical signs of a leak in a line under the concrete. If that is what you are seeing, read [slab leak detection in Mission Viejo](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection-mission-viejo.html).



**Inside walls and ceilings.** Supply lines to bathrooms, kitchens and laundry rooms run behind drywall, and in two-story homes a leak upstairs often first appears as a ceiling stain below.



**Irrigation and the line from the meter, especially on sloped lots.** Buried service and irrigation lines can leak for months with no sign indoors except the bill. Moulton Niguel Water District lists irrigation leaks and irrigation timer malfunctions among the reasons for a high-bill adjustment, which tells you how often it happens. A soggy patch, or a spot that stays green in a dry month, can point to it.



## Check for a leak yourself first



Turn off every faucet, appliance and irrigation zone, note the reading on your water meter, and check again after 30 minutes. If it moved, water is leaving the system somewhere. Our [water meter test guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html) walks through it, and [why is my water bill so high?](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-is-my-water-bill-so-high.html) covers the usual causes.



## Three water districts: whose side is the leak on?



The [City of Mission Viejo](https://www.missionviejo.gov/departments/public-works/water-conservation) says water is supplied to its residents by Moulton Niguel Water District, Santa Margarita Water District and El Toro Water District. Your bill shows which one serves you. A leak in the street or on the district's side of the meter goes to your district; Moulton Niguel's line is (949) 831-2500, answered 24/7 for emergencies, and Santa Margarita's customer care is (949) 459-6420. A leak on your side of the meter is generally the owner's to find and fix.



If a leak ran up your bill and you are a Moulton Niguel customer, its [Adjustment Request](https://www.mnwd.com/adjustments/) lists repair of a leak (a toilet, irrigation or a pinhole leak in the home) as a reason, asks for the form within 90 days of the high bill, and says approved adjustments are credited within two billing cycles. Santa Margarita and El Toro customers should ask their district about its policy. Keep your written findings and the repair invoice.

 Why do older Mission Viejo homes get leaks? +

 Does insurance pay for leak detection? +

## Where leaks show up in Laguna Beach homes



**Older supply piping.** The median Laguna Beach home was built in 1964 ([City-Stats, 2023 ACS data](https://city-stats.com/california/laguna-beach/housing)), so many homes are around 60 years old. Age alone doesn't mean a leak, but in an older system one pinhole is a reason to check the condition of the rest of the pipe.



**Buried lines on hillside and canyon lots.** On a sloped lot the service line from the meter and the irrigation lines can run a long way underground, and a leak there may show up only as a higher bill, a soggy patch downhill, or a spot that stays green in a dry month.



**Under the slab and inside walls.** Homes on concrete slabs can leak under the floor, with a warm spot or the sound of running water as the clue; in multi-level hillside homes a leak upstairs often first appears as a stain on the ceiling below. See [how we find slab leaks](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection.html).



## Why a slow leak matters more on a slope



Laguna Beach knows what water does to a hillside. On June 1, 2005, a landslide in Bluebird Canyon destroyed or severely damaged about 20 homes and about 350 were evacuated; early findings pointed to winter rains, and one resident described hearing her pipes rupture as the ground moved ([Insurance Journal](https://www.insurancejournal.com/magazines/mag-features/2005/06/20/57003.htm)). The same report notes a 1978 slide that cost 24 families their homes. A small plumbing leak does not mean a slope is failing, but water that keeps escaping into the ground is worth locating promptly. If you also see new cracks or ground movement, contact the City of Laguna Beach and a geotechnical professional; that is outside what a plumber can assess.



## Check for a leak yourself first



Laguna Beach County Water District's advice: turn off and leave off every tap inside and outside the home, record the meter reading, and check again in two to three hours. Many meters have a small red triangle that spins with even a small leak ([LBCWD FAQ](https://lbcwd.org/about-us/faq)). If the meter moved, water is leaving the system somewhere. Our [water meter test guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html) walks through it, and [why is my water bill so high?](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-is-my-water-bill-so-high.html) covers the usual causes.



## District side or your side?



Most of Laguna Beach, plus Emerald Bay, gets its water from [Laguna Beach County Water District](https://www.lbcwd.org/about-us/about-our-district); South Laguna is served by [South Coast Water District](https://bos5.oc.gov/district-resource/south-coast-water-district). Your bill names your district. Water coming up from the street, the meter box or a main is the district's to look at. A leak on your side of the meter is generally the owner's to find and fix, and LBCWD's permanent water-use rules list leaving a leaking pipe or fixture unrepaired as a prohibited use, so it pays to find it early.

 How we work


## Find the leak first, then a straight answer on the fix



 1 · Isolate

### Which line is leaking?

Pressure testing shows whether the hot line, cold line or the service line from the meter is losing water, so we know where to look.


 2 · Pinpoint

### Listen, trace and confirm

Acoustic equipment picks up the sound of pressurized water escaping, electronic locating traces where the pipe runs, and thermal imaging cross-checks hot-water leaks. The spot is marked for the smallest possible opening.


 3 · Decide

### Repair, reroute, or repipe

A single leak in a sound line is usually a spot repair. Repeat leaks in aging pipe may make a reroute or repipe the smarter call. We explain the trade-offs after diagnosis, never before.

 Who do I call about a leak at the street or the water meter in Laguna Beach? +


Call your water district. Most of Laguna Beach, plus Emerald Bay, is served by Laguna Beach County Water District; South Laguna is served by South Coast Water District. The name on your water bill tells you which one is yours. Water coming up from the street, the meter box or a main is the district's to look at. A leak on your side of the meter, in the line to the house, under the slab or inside a wall, is generally the property owner's to find and repair, and that is the part we locate.




 How do I check my Laguna Beach home for a hidden leak? +

 Can a leak on a hillside lot in Laguna Beach be serious? +


It can be. On June 1, 2005, a landslide in Bluebird Canyon destroyed or severely damaged about 20 homes and led to the evacuation of about 350; early findings blamed winter rains, and one resident described hearing her pipes rupture as the ground moved. A similar slide in 1978 cost 24 families their homes. A small leak does not mean a hillside is unstable, but water that keeps escaping into a slope is worth locating promptly.  Do older Laguna Beach homes get more leaks? +


Age is one factor. Age alone does not mean a home is leaking. One leak in an older system is a reason to check the condition of the rest of the pipe before choosing between a spot repair, a reroute or a repipe.




 Can you find a leak without tearing open walls or floors? +


In most cases, yes.  Does insurance pay for leak detection? +

## Where leaks show up in San Juan Capistrano homes



**Under the slab in 1970s to 1990s homes.** About two-thirds of San Juan Capistrano homes were built between 1970 and 1999 ([NeighborhoodScout](https://www.neighborhoodscout.com/ca/san-juan-capistrano/real-estate)), many on concrete slabs with copper supply lines underneath. A warm spot on the floor, the sound of running water with everything off, or a meter that won't stop are typical signs. More on [slab leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection.html).



**Long buried lines on large lots.** On equestrian and other large properties, water lines can run far underground to the house, a barn, a guest unit, troughs and irrigation. A leak there can run for months with no sign indoors except the bill, or a patch that stays green or soggy in a dry month. We test which line is losing water, then trace and listen along it to narrow the leak to one spot.



**Under manufactured homes.** About one in ten homes in the city is a mobile or manufactured home ([NeighborhoodScout](https://www.neighborhoodscout.com/ca/san-juan-capistrano/real-estate)). Their supply lines usually run in the crawlspace, so a leak shows up as soft flooring, a damp smell or water under the skirting rather than a warm slab.



**Inside walls and ceilings, and at worn fixtures.** Supply lines to bathrooms, kitchens and laundry rooms run behind drywall, and in two-story homes a leak upstairs often first appears as a ceiling stain below. San Juan Capistrano's water averages about 12 grains per gallon of hardness ([SMWD 2026 water quality report](https://www.smwd.com/DocumentCenter/View/6351/2026-Water-Quality-Report-ID-9---SJC)), and that scale wears water heaters, shutoff valves and faucet cartridges, so we check those too.



## Check for a leak yourself first



Turn off every faucet, appliance, irrigation zone and any automatic waterers, note the reading on your water meter, and check again after 30 minutes. If it moved, water is leaving the system somewhere. Our [water meter test guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html) walks through it. Since November 15, 2021, the Santa Margarita Water District has run San Juan Capistrano's water service ([Capistrano Dispatch](https://www.picketfencemedia.com/thecapistranodispatch/eye-on-sjc/one-year-later-a-look-at-santa-margarita-water-district-s-acquisition-of-san-juan/article_c7c7baee-a4df-588d-b826-65e81622c1a7.html)), so your SMWD bill history is a good place to spot an unexplained rise in use (see [why is my water bill so high?](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/why-is-my-water-bill-so-high.html)).

Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection does whole-house and partial PEX repiping in Laguna Niguel. Owner Lance answers the phone himself at [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).



## Repiping Laguna Niguel's copper-era homes



Much of Laguna Niguel was built in the 1970s–90s, and many of those homes still run their original copper water lines. Copper tends to wear throughout a system at the same rate, so when one section of an older line pinholes, other sections of the same age are often not far behind.



That's the point where homeowners start asking about a repipe: two or more slab leaks within a few years, corrosion at several fixtures, discolored water, or simply being tired of patching the same system. PEX resists the corrosion that causes those pinhole leaks, and its flexible runs need fewer fittings — fewer joints means fewer places for a future leak to start.



Not every home needs the whole system replaced. Sometimes a reroute of one problem line solves it. We test and inspect first, then tell you which applies — see [repair vs. reroute vs. repipe](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/repair-vs-reroute-vs-repipe.html).

- New shutoff valves and supply connections at fixtures

- Water restored at the end of each working day whenever possible

 Is PEX better than copper for older Laguna Niguel homes? +


For homes with aging copper, PEX is usually the better long-term choice: it doesn't corrode the way copper does, and its flexible runs need fewer fittings, which means fewer places for a leak to start. It's also certified for drinking water and standard in new residential construction.

## Slab leaks in San Clemente homes



San Clemente's homes span a century. Near the pier and downtown you'll find older Spanish-style houses, many with original copper; east of the 5, neighborhoods like Forster Ranch and Talega are newer, typically built on concrete slabs with copper water lines run under the concrete. A slab leak can happen in either.



Newer doesn't mean immune. In 2015 a lawsuit over the 3,800-home Talega community claimed its copper pipe was prone to leaks under local water conditions ([PHCP Pros](https://www.phcppros.com/articles/657-lawsuit-blames-california-home-builders-for-leaks-from-copper-pipes)), and ABC7 reported pinhole-leak claims over 2003–2013 homes in nearby Ladera Ranch ([ABC7](https://abc7.com/post/oc-homes-could-face-possible-damaging-leaks-from-holes-in-pipes/1208620/)). Those are claims, not findings about your house — the only way to know is to test it.



Water supply matters too. Most of the city is served by the City of San Clemente's utility, Talega by Santa Margarita Water District, and parts of north San Clemente by South Coast Water District. The water is hard, so scale shows up in water heaters and fixtures. If you suspect a leak, start with the [30-minute water meter test](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html): a meter that keeps moving with every fixture and irrigation zone off means water is escaping somewhere.

## Ladera Ranch's copper pinhole-leak history



Ladera Ranch broke ground in 1999, so most homes are newer than the rest of South Orange County. Even so, starting in 2013 hundreds of Ladera Ranch homeowners sued their builders over pinhole leaks in copper water pipes. Settlements reached in 2015 and 2016 paid toward PEX repiping or epoxy pipe treatment for covered homes built between May 2003 and May 2013 ([ABC7, 2016](https://abc7.com/post/oc-homes-could-face-possible-damaging-leaks-from-holes-in-pipes/1208620/); [plaintiffs' counsel, 2015](https://www.bridgfordlaw.com/news/bridgford-gleason-artinian-llp-secures-win-for-ladera-homeowners-in-copper-pipe-suit/)).



The cause was never settled as a finding. Homeowners argued the copper was not suited to the local water; builders said there was no defect in the pipe itself. A separate class action against the water districts was dismissed in 2015, with the court ruling that districts following state and federal disinfectant standards could not be sued ([report of the July 2015 ruling](https://www.bridgfordlaw.com/news/judge-tosses-out-lawsuit-on-south-county-copper-pipe-leaks/)). Ladera Ranch water is supplied by the [Santa Margarita Water District](https://smwd.com/627/Water-Quality-Ladera-Ranch).



What that means for you: if your home still has its original copper and you have had one pinhole leak, another one is worth planning for. If a previous owner already repiped with PEX, leaks are more likely to come from fittings, fixture connections, the water heater or irrigation lines.



 Repiping services in Ladera Ranch



- Whole-house copper-to-PEX repiping

- Partial repipes and reroutes for one failing line

- [Leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html) and [slab leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection.html) before any repipe decision

- Pinhole leak repair when a spot fix is the right call

- Shutoff valve rebuilds and supply line replacement

- Water restored at the end of each working day whenever possible




## Still have copper? A 2-minute check



Open the cabinet under a kitchen or bathroom sink and look where the supply pipes leave the wall, then look at the pipes on top of your water heater. Reddish-brown metal is copper. Flexible plastic tubing in red, blue or white is PEX. Green or blue crust on copper fittings is worth mentioning when you call.



More on [how PEX repiping works](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping.html), [copper vs. PEX](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/copper-vs-pex-pipes.html), [repair vs. reroute vs. repipe](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/repair-vs-reroute-vs-repipe.html), and [plumbing in Ladera Ranch](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/cities/ladera-ranch.html).

 Ladera Ranch repiping FAQ


## Common questions from Ladera Ranch homeowners



 Who handles PEX repiping in Ladera Ranch? +


Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection does whole-house and partial PEX repiping in Ladera Ranch. We're an owner-operated company based nearby in Laguna Niguel, we locate and diagnose leaks before recommending a repipe, and owner Lance answers the phone at [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).




 Are pinhole leaks common in Ladera Ranch homes? +


They have been. Starting in 2013, hundreds of Ladera Ranch homeowners sued their builders over pinhole leaks in copper water pipes, and settlements in 2015 and 2016 paid toward PEX repiping or epoxy pipe treatment for covered homes built between May 2003 and May 2013. The cause was disputed: homeowners argued the copper was not suited to the local water, builders said the pipe itself was not defective, and a 2015 court ruling dismissed a separate suit against the water districts.




 What causes pinhole leaks in copper pipes? +


Pinhole leaks come from pitting corrosion, where small spots on the inside of a copper pipe wear through while the rest of the pipe looks fine. Water chemistry, water velocity and installation quality are all factors that have been argued. In Ladera Ranch the cause was contested in court and never settled as a finding, so we diagnose each home on its own evidence.




 How do I know if my Ladera Ranch home still has copper pipes? +


Look at the pipes where they come out of the wall under a kitchen or bathroom sink and at the water heater connections. Copper is reddish-brown metal; PEX is flexible plastic tubing, usually red, blue or white. Many Ladera Ranch homes were repiped with PEX after the lawsuits, so a previous owner may already have done it. If you are not sure, we can check during a visit.




 Do I need a whole-house repipe after one pinhole leak in Ladera Ranch? +


Not necessarily. A single leak can often be repaired or a line rerouted. Repeat pinhole leaks in different spots, a leak under the slab, or green or blue staining on exposed copper are signs the system as a whole is wearing, and that is when a whole-house PEX repipe is worth comparing against further repairs. We locate the leak first and lay out both options.




 Is PEX better than copper for Ladera Ranch homes? +


PEX does not corrode the way copper does, and its flexible runs need fewer fittings inside walls. That removes the pitting corrosion behind most pinhole leaks, though no plumbing is leak-proof forever, and fittings, fixture connections and water heaters still need attention. Our copper vs. PEX guide covers the trade-offs.




 Can I still file a claim under the Ladera Ranch copper pipe settlements? +


The settlements we found reported on were from 2015 and 2016 and had limited claim windows, so they are unlikely to still be open. We are plumbers, not attorneys: if you think your home was covered, check your purchase or HOA records or ask an attorney. Whatever the answer, we can document the leak and the condition of your pipes for you.




 How long does a repipe take in Ladera Ranch? +


Most residential repipes take one to a few days depending on the size of the home and access, with water restored at the end of each working day whenever possible.
